title: Compatible strict henselization core data without final residue square
statement: The compatible strict henselization rings, maps, universal homeomorphisms, structural equalities and residue factorizations exist.

proof.text: Apply exists_compatibleStrictHenselizationCoreExistence to obtain A, B, their henselian structures, separably closed residue fields, spectrum presentations, universal-homeomorphism residue maps and residue factorizations. Associate h_iota after composition with nu to obtain s = t followed by g. Apply exists_compatibleStrictHenselizationCoreCompletion to these presentations, obtaining the local ring map and structural equality. Assemble the unchanged witnesses and these three equalities. This is the existing upstream proof on strictLocalization; the sole DAG parent already uses that presentation.

lean.statement:
theorem Etale.exists_compatibleStrictHenselizationCoreData
    {S T : Scheme.{u}} {g : T ⟶ S}
    {k k' Ω : Type u} [Field k] [IsSepClosed k] [Field k'] [IsSepClosed k']
    [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (σ : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S) (τ : Spec (.of k') ⟶ T)
    (ι : Spec (.of k') ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (hι : ι ≫ σ = τ ≫ g)
    (hσ : ∃ (s : S) (ψ : S.residueField s ⟶ .of k),
      ψ.hom.IsIntegral ∧ Spec.map ψ ≫ S.fromSpecResidueField s = σ)
    (hτ : ∃ (t : T) (ψ : T.residueField t ⟶ .of k'),
      ψ.hom.IsIntegral ∧ Spec.map ψ ≫ T.fromSpecResidueField t = τ)
    (ν : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec (.of k')) :
    let s := ν ≫ ι ≫ σ
    let t := ν ≫ τ
    ∃ (A B : Type u) (cA : CommRing A) (cB : CommRing B),
      letI := cA
      letI := cB
      ∃ (hA : HenselianLocalRing A) (hB : HenselianLocalRing B),
        letI := hA
        letI := hB
        ∃ (sA : IsSepClosed (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A))
          (sB : IsSepClosed (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B)),
          letI := sA
          letI := sB
          ∃ (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : IsLocalHom φ),
            letI := hφ
            ∃ (eA : Spec (.of A) ≅ strictLocalization s)
              (eB : Spec (.of B) ≅ strictLocalization t)
              (ρA : Spec (.of k) ⟶ Spec (.of (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)))
              (ρB : Spec (.of k') ⟶ Spec (.of (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B))),
              IsUniversalHomeomorphism ρA ∧ IsUniversalHomeomorphism ρB ∧
              Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ) ≫ eA.hom ≫
                strictLocalizationToBase s =
                eB.hom ≫ strictLocalizationToBase t ≫ g ∧
              ρA ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (IsLocalRing.residue A)) ≫
                eA.hom ≫ strictLocalizationToBase s = σ ∧
              ρB ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (IsLocalRing.residue B)) ≫
                eB.hom ≫ strictLocalizationToBase t = τ

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $g:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes, let $k,k'$ be separably closed fields and $\Omega$ an algebraically closed
field. Let $\sigma:\operatorname{Spec}k\to S$, $\tau:\operatorname{Spec}k'\to T$ and
$\iota:\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ satisfy $\sigma\circ\iota=g\circ\tau$. Assume that $\sigma$
factors as $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_0)\to S$ for a point $s_0\in S$ with
$\kappa(s_0)\to k$ integral, and that $\tau$ factors likewise through $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t_0)$ for a point
$t_0\in T$ with $\kappa(t_0)\to k'$ integral. Let $\nu:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$ and
consider the geometric points $\bar s=\sigma\iota\nu$ of $S$ and $\bar t=\tau\nu$ of $T$, with strict localizations
$\pi_{\bar s}:S_{(\bar s)}\to S$ and $\pi_{\bar t}:T_{(\bar t)}\to T$.

Then there exist henselian local rings $A$ and $B$ with separably closed residue fields $\kappa_A$ and $\kappa_B$,
a local homomorphism $\varphi:A\to B$, isomorphisms $e_A:\operatorname{Spec}A\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{(\bar s)}$ and
$e_B:\operatorname{Spec}B\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{(\bar t)}$, and morphisms
$\rho_A:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_A$ and $\rho_B:\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_B$
such that

- **(a)** $\rho_A$ and $\rho_B$ are universal homeomorphisms;
- **(b)** $\pi_{\bar s}\circ e_A\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi=g\circ\pi_{\bar t}\circ e_B$;
- **(c)** $\pi_{\bar s}\circ e_A\circ\operatorname{Spec}(A\to\kappa_A)\circ\rho_A=\sigma$ and
  $\pi_{\bar t}\circ e_B\circ\operatorname{Spec}(B\to\kappa_B)\circ\rho_B=\tau$.

The compatibility of $\rho_A,\rho_B$ with $\iota$ and the residue map of $\varphi$ is not asserted.

proof.text:
Let $A$ and $B$ be the colimits of the coordinate rings of the affine pointed étale neighbourhoods of $\bar s$ and
$\bar t$; their spectra are the strict localizations, which gives $e_A$ and $e_B$. Each is a strictly henselian
local ring whose residue field is the separable closure of the residue field of the image point inside $\Omega$
(Stacks Project, Tags 04HX and 03PS). Since $k$ and $k'$ are separably closed, these separable closures lie in the
images of $k$ and $k'$, which gives $\rho_A$, $\rho_B$ and the equalities (c). The integrality hypotheses make $k$
and $k'$ algebraic over the residue fields of $s_0$ and $t_0$, so $k$ and $k'$ are purely inseparable over
$\kappa_A$ and $\kappa_B$, and $\rho_A$, $\rho_B$ are universal homeomorphisms (Tag 04DY). Functoriality of strict
henselization (Tag 04GU), applied to $\sigma\iota\nu=g\tau\nu$, gives the local homomorphism $\varphi$ and the
square (b).
